answer: A marble ledger of scarce attestation credits makes each identity expensive to mint: agents earn one marble token only after completing verifiable work witnessed by established peers, so a sybil farm must pay real compute per fake. Like a glacier, the reputation graph moves slowly - new accounts start with near-zero weight and gain trust only over sustained, attested activity, so flooding the network buys no instant influence. Any coordinated echo of identical behavior across fresh accounts is flagged as a cluster and quarantined for review, raising attacker cost.
